data.narrative:
AlixLabs is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Jonas Sundqvist, Dmitry Suyatin, and Amin Karimi that has raised €15M to date. The chips & semiconductors sector includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers such as SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Etched, though none provide sufficient calibration data for traditional peer multiples.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology proves most applicable. Using total raised (€15M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement yields €30M. Public-comp anchoring, while theoretically relevant—the Semiconductors sector trades at a 21.5x median price-to-sales multiple across the three public tickers—cannot be executed without AlixLabs' revenue figures, which private companies rarely disclose. Peer-median triangulation is similarly inapplicable; while 12 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar-valuation-tier) produced insufficient datapoints to support a reliable multiple.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €26M–€34M (median €30M), grounded in one method. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data, limiting comparable-company and public-market anchoring; the thinness of narrow-peer data for semiconductor-specific stage multiples; and reliance on raised capital as a proxy for fundamental value. Additional commercial traction metrics would materially refine this estimate.
